cli.help.accounts:
Accounts
  clm --list                     number, name, folder and e-mail of the accounts
  clm --usage                    5h and 7d quotas of each account
  clm --add [name]               new account, sign-in in the browser,
                                 to be finished by a person
  clm --rename <account> <name>  renames, no comma and no name already taken
  clm --move <account> <rank>    changes its place in the menu, 1 at the top
  clm --remove <account> --yes   removes from the menu, the folder stays
  clm --remove <account> --erase --yes
                                 removes and erases the account folder,
                                 after an archive in Downloads
  clm --save[=name,name]         archive of accounts in Downloads
  clm --backups                  archives found, the most recent first
  clm --restore=<archive> [--only=name,name] [--yes]
                                 restores accounts, the current state is
                                 archived first; --yes accepts the hooks,
                                 MCP, env and permissions that change
cli.help.display:
Display of this PC
  clm --palette auto|dark|light  menu colours, auto follows the system
  clm --anim auto|on|off         menu animations, auto follows the system
  clm --usage-poll 15..600       delay between two API reads, 30 s
cli.help.drive:
Drive
  clm --drive-status             connection, PC name, auto sync,
                                 last sync
  clm --drive-login              connects this PC to Google Drive, then
                                 asks for the sync phrase
  clm --sync-key                 enters the sync phrase on this PC
  clm --sync-key-reset           new sync phrase for all the PCs
  clm --sync-key-forget          forgets the sync phrase on this PC
  clm --sync                     Drive sync right now
  clm --sync --force             same, beyond the safeguard on deletions
  clm --sync-auto=on|off         sync at launch and when Claude closes
cli.help.files:
Files of clm, one folder per user
  Windows                        %LOCALAPPDATA%\clm
  Linux                          ~/.local/state/clm, or $XDG_STATE_HOME/clm
  macOS                          ~/Library/Application Support/clm
  accounts.json                  list of accounts, names and folders
  sync-choice.json               sync settings of this PC
  sync-catalog.json              skills and MCP seen at the last sync
  drive.json                     Drive connection, secret, do not share
  display.json                   colours, animations, API delay of this PC
  The old .claude-accounts.json and .clm-*.json of the home folder are
  moved there at the first launch.
cli.help.homeFiles:
Files of the home folder
  .local/bin                     clm scripts and clm.version
cli.help.intro:
clm: Claude Code accounts, quotas, updates and Google Drive sync

With no option, clm opens the menu. Every option below works without the menu,
for a person as well as for a script or an agent, and exits with code 0 if
all goes well, 1 otherwise. An <account> is given by its number in the menu
(1 to 9), its name or its folder.
cli.help.launch:
Launch
  clm                            account menu
  clm -N [arguments]             launches account N (1 to 9) without the menu,
                                 the arguments go to Claude Code
  clm --no-update                updates neither clm nor Claude Code
  clm --web                      menu, and its web page in the browser:
                                 accounts, Drive, display, archives
  clm --help, -h                 this help
cli.help.menuInstall: installs the announced new version of clm
cli.help.prefs:
Sync settings of this PC, Drive connected
  clm --prefs                    skills and MCP, ticked or not, with their id
  clm --prefs-on <id> [<id>...]  tick: synced on this PC
  clm --prefs-off <id> [<id>...] untick: removed from this PC, kept elsewhere
  clm --prefs-erase <id> [<id>...] --yes
                                 erases everywhere at the next sync
  An id is written skill:<name>, mcp:<project>|<name> or global:<name>, in
  quotes because of the |, or shortens to the name alone if it is unique.
  "skill:*" targets all the skills and "mcp:*" all the MCP, global ones
  included, in quotes because of the * ; [-] means a partly ticked group,
  and a group cannot be erased.
  --prefs-on also cancels a requested erase. After a change, clm starts
  the sync. Local MCP (~/.mcp.json and projects under the home folder)
  follow the boxes. Global MCP (mcpServers at the top of .claude.json)
  never go to the other PCs and are copied between the accounts of this
  PC: unticking them removes them from all those accounts.
cli.help.updates:
Updates
  clm --version                  versions of clm and Claude Code
  clm --update                   updates clm, then Claude Code of each
                                 account
cli.help.variables:
Variables
  CLM_ANIM=0|1                   turns the menu animations off or on,
                                 before --anim
  STATUSLINE_BG=dark|light       sets the palette, before --palette
